coverage.scope: Selected official-source chronology, not a census of all events or reports.
coverage.review: AI-assisted source-reading curation; local draft pending user review.

notes.title: US exports slumped as trading partners entered recession
notes.summary: The FOMC reported a slump in US exports as several major trading partners also entered recession.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2009-03-18
source.quote: U.S. exports have slumped as a number of major trading partners have also fallen into recession.

notes.title: Job losses and tight credit weighed on spending
notes.summary: The FOMC linked weak consumer sentiment and spending to job losses, falling equity and housing wealth, and tight credit conditions.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2009-03-18
source.quote: Job losses, declining equity and housing wealth, and tight credit conditions have weighed on consumer sentiment and spending.

notes.title: Treasury purchases announced to support credit markets
notes.summary: The Committee decided to purchase up to $300 billion of longer-term Treasury securities over the following six months.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2009-03-18
source.quote: the Committee decided to purchase up to $300 billion of longer-term Treasury securities over the next six months.

notes.title: Household spending recovered gradually under constraints
notes.summary: The FOMC reported gradually increasing household spending, constrained by unemployment, modest income growth, lower housing wealth and tight credit.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2010-11-03
source.quote: Household spending is increasing gradually, but remains constrained by high unemployment, modest income growth, lower housing wealth, and tight credit.

notes.title: A further $600 billion of Treasury purchases planned
notes.summary: The Committee intended to buy a further $600 billion of longer-term Treasuries by the end of Q2 2011.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2010-11-03
source.quote: the Committee intends to purchase a further $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities by the end of the second quarter of 2011

notes.title: Longer-maturity Treasury purchases planned
notes.summary: The Committee intended to purchase $400 billion of Treasuries with remaining maturities of 6–30 years by end-June 2012, as part of its maturity-extension programme.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2011-09-21
source.quote: The Committee intends to purchase, by the end of June 2012, $400 billion of Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 6 years to 30 years

notes.title: Additional mortgage-backed purchases announced
notes.summary: The Committee agreed to purchase additional agency mortgage-backed securities at $40 billion per month.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2012-09-13
source.quote: the Committee agreed today to increase policy accommodation by purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month.

notes.title: Fiscal restraint accompanied a strengthening housing sector
notes.summary: The FOMC reported advancing household spending and investment and a stronger housing sector, while assessing that fiscal policy was restraining growth.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2013-06-19
source.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, and the housing sector has strengthened further, but fiscal policy is restraining economic growth.

notes.title: Economic activity rebounded and labour indicators improved
notes.summary: The FOMC reported a rebound in economic activity and generally improving labour-market indicators.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2014-06-18
source.quote: growth in economic activity has rebounded in recent months. Labor market indicators generally showed further improvement.

notes.title: A stronger projected dollar lowered the staff growth forecast
notes.summary: Fed staff revised down its medium-term real GDP growth forecast, mostly because of a higher projected foreign-exchange value of the dollar.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2015-03-18
source.quote: The staff's medium-term forecast for real GDP growth also was revised down, mostly because of the effects of a higher projected path for the foreign exchange value of the dollar.

notes.title: Global developments posed growth and inflation headwinds
notes.summary: The FOMC judged that recent global economic and financial developments might restrain US activity and were likely to push inflation lower in the near term.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2015-09-17
source.quote: Recent global economic and financial developments may restrain economic activity somewhat and are likely to put further downward pressure on inflation in the near term.

notes.title: Labour improvement slowed as activity appeared to pick up
notes.summary: The FOMC reported slower improvement in the labour market, alongside an apparent pickup in economic activity.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2016-06-15
source.quote: the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in economic activity appears to have picked up.

notes.title: Balance-sheet normalization set to begin in October
notes.summary: The Committee announced that its previously described balance-sheet normalization programme would start in October 2017.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2017-09-20
source.quote: In October, the Committee will initiate the balance sheet normalization program described in the June 2017 Addendum to the Committee's Policy Normalization Principles and Plans.

notes.title: Moderate growth expected with gradual policy adjustments
notes.summary: With further gradual adjustments in monetary policy, the FOMC expected moderate medium-term growth and strong labour-market conditions.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2018-03-21
source.quote: The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace in the medium term and labor market conditions will remain strong.

notes.title: Committee adopted patient guidance on future rate adjustments
notes.summary: The FOMC said it would be patient in deciding which future adjustments to the federal funds target range might be appropriate.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2019-01-30
source.quote: the Committee will be patient as it determines what future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate

notes.title: Asset purchases linked to market-functioning needs
notes.summary: The Federal Reserve announced continued Treasury and agency mortgage-backed purchases in the amounts needed to support smooth market functioning.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2020-03-23
source.quote: The Federal Reserve will continue to purchase Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities in the amounts needed to support smooth market functioning

notes.title: Framework allowed a likely period of above-2% inflation
notes.summary: The revised strategy said that, after persistently below-2% inflation, appropriate policy would likely aim for moderately above-2% inflation for some time.

source.title: FOMC strategy update — 2020-08-27
source.section: Changes to the monetary policy framework
source.quote: following periods when inflation has been running persistently below 2 percent, appropriate monetary policy will likely aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time.

notes.title: Activity and employment strengthened during reopening
notes.summary: The FOMC reported stronger economic activity and employment alongside strong policy support. Sectors hit hardest by the pandemic remained weak but were improving.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2021-06-16
source.quote: Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak but have shown improvement.

notes.title: Balance-sheet reductions scheduled for June
notes.summary: The Committee decided to begin reducing Treasury, agency-debt and agency mortgage-backed holdings on 1 June 2022.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2022-05-04
source.quote: the Committee decided to begin reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities on June 1

notes.title: Future rate increases would account for tightening already delivered
notes.summary: The FOMC said the pace of future rate increases would take account of cumulative tightening, policy transmission lags, and economic and financial developments.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2022-11-02
source.quote: In determining the pace of future increases in the target range, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.

notes.title: Tighter credit was expected, with uncertain effects
notes.summary: The FOMC expected recent developments to tighten credit for households and businesses and weigh on activity, hiring and inflation; the magnitude was uncertain.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2023-03-22
source.quote: Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects is uncertain.

notes.title: Rate cuts required greater confidence in sustainable disinflation
notes.summary: The Committee did not expect rate cuts to be appropriate before it had greater confidence that inflation was moving sustainably toward 2%.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2024-03-20
source.quote: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.

notes.title: Target range cut to 4.25–4.50%
notes.summary: The Committee lowered the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage point to 4.25–4.50%.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2024-12-18
source.quote: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.

notes.title: Risks of higher unemployment and inflation rose
notes.summary: The Committee judged that risks of both higher unemployment and higher inflation had increased.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2025-05-07
source.quote: The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that the risks of higher unemployment and higher inflation have risen.

notes.title: Strong productivity and investment accompanied stable unemployment
notes.summary: The FOMC reported strong productivity growth and capital investment; job gains had kept pace with the workforce and unemployment had changed little.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2026-10-28
source.quote: Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

notes.title: Main refinancing rate cut to 1%
notes.summary: The ECB decided to lower the main refinancing rate by 25 basis points to 1.00%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the main refinancing operations of the Eurosystem will be decreased by 25 basis points to 1.00%

notes.title: Staff projected a deep contraction in 2009
notes.summary: Eurosystem staff projected real GDP growth between −5.1% and −4.1% in 2009, followed by between −1.0% and 0.4% in 2010.

source.title: Introductory statement with Q&A
source.quote: annual real GDP growth will range between -5.1% and -4.1% in 2009 and between -1.0% and 0.4% in 2010.

notes.title: Inflation was expected to turn temporarily negative
notes.summary: The ECB projected annual inflation rates declining further and remaining negative temporarily over the coming months, citing base effects.

source.title: Introductory statement with Q&A
source.quote: Looking ahead, owing to these base effects, annual inflation rates are projected to decline further and temporarily remain negative over the coming months,

notes.title: Securities Markets Programme announced
notes.summary: The ECB announced interventions in euro area public and private debt securities markets through the Securities Markets Programme.

source.title: ECB decides on measures to address severe tensions in financial markets
source.quote: To conduct interventions in the euro area public and private debt securities markets (Securities Markets Programme)

notes.title: Economic recovery retained positive momentum
notes.summary: The ECB assessed that recent data and surveys generally confirmed continuing positive underlying momentum in the euro area recovery.

source.title: Introductory statement with Q&A
source.quote: Recent statistical releases and survey-based evidence generally confirm that the positive underlying momentum of the economic recovery in the euro area remains in place.

notes.title: Main refinancing rate raised to 1.50%
notes.summary: The ECB decided to raise the main refinancing rate by 25 basis points to 1.50%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the main refinancing operations of the Eurosystem will be increased by 25 basis points to 1.50%

notes.title: Three-year refinancing operations introduced
notes.summary: The ECB announced two longer-term refinancing operations with a 36-month maturity and an option for early repayment after one year.

source.title: ECB announces measures to support bank lending and money market activity
source.quote: To conduct two longer-term refinancing operations (LTROs) with a maturity of 36 months and the option of early repayment after one year.

notes.title: Deposit facility rate cut to zero
notes.summary: The ECB decided to reduce the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 0.00%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the deposit facility will be decreased by 25 basis points to 0.00%

notes.title: OMT framework required programme conditionality
notes.summary: The ECB set out the Outright Monetary Transactions framework, requiring strict and effective conditionality under an appropriate EFSF/ESM programme. This was a framework, not an announcement that purchases had begun.

source.title: Technical features of Outright Monetary Transactions
source.quote: A necessary condition for Outright Monetary Transactions is strict and effective conditionality attached to an appropriate European Financial Stability Facility/European Stability Mechanism (EFSF/ESM) programme.

notes.title: Rates expected to remain low for an extended period
notes.summary: The ECB expected key interest rates to remain at their present or lower levels for an extended period.

source.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
source.quote: The Governing Council expects the key ECB interest rates to remain at present or lower levels for an extended period of time.

notes.title: Main refinancing rate cut to 0.25%
notes.summary: The ECB decided to lower the main refinancing rate by 25 basis points to 0.25%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the main refinancing operations of the Eurosystem will be decreased by 25 basis points to 0.25%

notes.title: Deposit facility rate moved below zero
notes.summary: The ECB decided to cut the deposit facility rate by 10 basis points to −0.10%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the deposit facility will be decreased by 10 basis points to -0.10%

notes.title: Expanded asset purchases announced at €60 billion monthly
notes.summary: The ECB announced an expanded asset purchase programme with combined monthly purchases of €60 billion.

source.title: ECB announces expanded asset purchase programme
source.quote: Combined monthly asset purchases to amount to €60 billion

notes.title: Monthly asset purchases expanded to €80 billion
notes.summary: The ECB decided to expand monthly asset purchases to €80 billion from April 2016.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The monthly purchases under the asset purchase programme will be expanded to €80 billion starting in April.

notes.title: Deposit facility rate cut to −0.40%
notes.summary: The ECB decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 10 basis points to −0.40%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the deposit facility will be decreased by 10 basis points to -0.40%

notes.title: Staff projected very low inflation in 2016
notes.summary: ECB staff projected annual HICP inflation at 0.1% in 2016, 1.3% in 2017 and 1.6% in 2018.

source.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
source.quote: which foresee annual HICP inflation at 0.1% in 2016, 1.3% in 2017 and 1.6% in 2018.

notes.title: Net asset purchases intended to slow from January 2018
notes.summary: The ECB intended to continue net asset purchases at a reduced monthly pace of €30 billion from January 2018.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: From January 2018 the net asset purchases are intended to continue at a monthly pace of €30 billion

notes.title: Underlying inflation expected to rise gradually
notes.summary: The ECB expected underlying euro area inflation to rise gradually over the medium term.

source.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
source.quote: Underlying inflation in the euro area is expected to continue to rise gradually over the medium term,

notes.title: Net asset purchases set to end in December
notes.summary: The ECB announced that net purchases under the asset purchase programme would end in December 2018.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: the net purchases under the asset purchase programme (APP) will end in December 2018.

notes.title: Staff projected slower growth after 2018
notes.summary: Eurosystem staff projected annual real GDP growth of 1.9% in 2018, 1.7% in both 2019 and 2020, and 1.5% in 2021.

source.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
source.quote: These projections foresee annual real GDP increasing by 1.9% in 2018, 1.7% in 2019, 1.7% in 2020 and 1.5% in 2021.

notes.title: Deposit facility rate cut to −0.50%
notes.summary: The ECB decided to reduce the deposit facility rate by 10 basis points to −0.50%.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The interest rate on the deposit facility will be decreased by 10 basis points to -0.50%.

notes.title: Net asset purchases restarted
notes.summary: The ECB announced a restart of net asset purchases at €20 billion per month from 1 November 2019.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: Net purchases will be restarted under the Governing Council’s asset purchase programme (APP) at a monthly pace of €20 billion as from 1 November.

notes.title: €750 billion pandemic purchase programme launched
notes.summary: The ECB announced the Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme with an initial envelope of €750 billion.

source.title: ECB announces €750 billion Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme (PEPP)
source.quote: This new Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme (PEPP) will have an overall envelope of €750 billion.

notes.title: Pandemic purchase envelope increased to €1,850 billion
notes.summary: The ECB decided to increase the PEPP envelope by €500 billion, bringing the announced total to €1,850 billion.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: the Governing Council decided to increase the envelope of the pandemic emergency purchase programme (PEPP) by €500 billion to a total of €1,850 billion.

notes.title: New strategy set a symmetric 2% inflation target
notes.summary: The ECB published a new strategy adopting a symmetric 2% inflation target over the medium term.

source.title: ECB’s Governing Council approves its new monetary policy strategy
source.quote: New strategy adopts symmetric 2% inflation target over medium term

notes.title: Interest-rate forward guidance revised
notes.summary: The ECB revised its interest-rate forward guidance to underline its commitment to a persistently accommodative stance in pursuit of its inflation target.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: the Governing Council today revised its forward guidance on interest rates. It did so to underline its commitment to maintain a persistently accommodative monetary policy stance to meet its inflation target.

notes.title: Key interest rates raised by 50 basis points
notes.summary: The ECB decided to raise its three key interest rates by 50 basis points.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The Governing Council decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 50 basis points

notes.title: Inflation expected to remain above target for an extended period
notes.summary: The ECB assessed that inflation was far too high and likely to stay above target for an extended period.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: inflation remains far too high and is likely to stay above target for an extended period.

notes.title: Key interest rates raised by 75 basis points
notes.summary: The ECB decided to raise its three key interest rates by 75 basis points.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 75 basis points.

notes.title: Staff projected weak euro area growth
notes.summary: ECB staff expected euro area growth of 0.7% in 2023, 1.0% in 2024 and 1.5% in 2025.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: They now expect the euro area economy to expand by 0.7% in 2023, 1.0% in 2024 and 1.5% in 2025.

notes.title: Staff projected inflation above target through 2025
notes.summary: ECB staff projected average inflation of 5.6% in 2023, 3.2% in 2024 and 2.1% in 2025.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: average inflation at 5.6% in 2023, 3.2% in 2024 and 2.1% in 2025.

notes.title: Key interest rates raised by a further 25 basis points
notes.summary: The ECB decided to raise the three key interest rates by 25 basis points.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: the Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

notes.title: Domestic price pressures remained strong
notes.summary: The ECB assessed that domestic price pressures remained strong amid elevated wage growth, with inflation likely to stay above target well into 2025.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: domestic price pressures remain strong as wage growth is elevated, and inflation is likely to stay above target well into next year.

notes.title: Key interest rates cut by 25 basis points
notes.summary: The ECB decided to lower its three key interest rates by 25 basis points.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The Governing Council today decided to lower the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

notes.title: Staff projected a gradual increase in growth
notes.summary: Eurosystem staff projected real GDP growth averaging 0.9% in 2025, 1.1% in 2026 and 1.3% in 2027.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: Staff see real GDP growth averaging 0.9% in 2025, 1.1% in 2026 and 1.3% in 2027.

notes.title: Key interest rates lowered again
notes.summary: The ECB decided to lower its three key interest rates by 25 basis points.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: The Governing Council today decided to lower the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

notes.title: Trade-policy uncertainty expected to weigh on investment and exports
notes.summary: The ECB expected uncertainty around trade policies to weigh on business investment and exports, especially in the short term.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: the uncertainty surrounding trade policies is expected to weigh on business investment and exports, especially in the short term,

notes.title: Staff projected inflation returning toward 2% by 2028
notes.summary: Eurosystem staff projected headline inflation averaging 3.0% in 2026, 2.3% in 2027 and 2.0% in 2028 in their baseline.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: headline inflation is expected to average 3.0% in 2026, 2.3% in 2027 and 2.0% in 2028.

notes.title: Key interest rates raised by 25 basis points
notes.summary: The ECB decided to raise its three key interest rates by 25 basis points.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: it today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

notes.title: Higher energy prices posed opposing risks to inflation and growth
notes.summary: The ECB assessed that rising energy prices posed upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth.

source.title: Monetary policy decisions
source.quote: Energy prices have continued to rise, posing upside risks to the inflation outlook and downside risks to the growth outlook.

notes.title: Consumer price inflation had fallen to 6.1%
notes.summary: The OECD reported Turkish consumer price inflation falling from 11.9% in October 2008 to 6.1% in April 2009.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2009 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual OECD Countries > Turkey
source.quote: Consumer price inflation fell from 11.9% in October to 6.1% in April

notes.title: OECD projected a strong rebound in 2010
notes.summary: The OECD projected Turkish GDP growth of 6.8% in 2010 and 4.5% in 2011.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2010 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual Member Countries > Turkey
source.quote: GDP is projected to grow by 6.8% in 2010 and 4.5% in 2011.

notes.title: Fiscal stimulus had been withdrawn
notes.summary: The OECD reported that the 2009 countercyclical fiscal stimulus was withdrawn in 2010 and the headline fiscal balance improved further in 2011.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2011 Issue 2 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual OECD Countries > Turkey
source.quote: The countercyclical fiscal stimulus imparted in 2009 was withdrawn in 2010, and the headline fiscal balance improved further in 2011.

notes.title: Gradual recovery expected as confidence improved
notes.summary: The OECD projected a gradual recovery in Turkish growth during 2012 as confidence and international conditions improved.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2012 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual OECD Countries > Turkey
source.quote: Growth is projected to recover gradually in 2012 as confidence and international conditions improve

notes.title: Inflation and the external deficit remained elevated
notes.summary: The OECD judged that inflation and the current account deficit remained above comfortable levels.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2013 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual OECD Countries > Turkey
source.quote: Inflation and the current account deficit both remain above comfort levels, however.

notes.title: One-week repo rate raised to 10%
notes.summary: The CBRT Monetary Policy Committee increased the one-week repo rate from 4.5% to 10%.

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2014-06)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee
source.quote: One-week repo rate is increased from 4.5 percent to 10 percent.

notes.title: OECD linked political tensions to tighter financial conditions
notes.summary: The OECD described political tensions as denting confidence, provoking capital outflows and forcing sharp interest-rate increases in early 2014.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2014 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual OECD Countries > Turkey
source.quote: Political tensions have dented confidence, provoking capital outflows and forcing the central bank to raise interest rates sharply in early 2014.

notes.title: Growth weakened again in early 2015
notes.summary: The OECD reported that growth weakened in early 2015 after a short-lived upturn in late 2014.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2015 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 2. Developments in Individual OECD Countries and Selected Non-Member Economies > Turkey
source.quote: Growth weakened in early 2015, after a short-lived upturn in late 2014.

notes.title: Growth projected to stay near 4%
notes.summary: The OECD projected Turkish GDP growth close to 4% per year in 2016 and 2017.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2016 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 3. Developments in Individual OECD and Selected Non-Member Economies > Turkey
source.quote: GDP growth is projected to remain close to 4% per annum in 2016 and 2017.

notes.title: Double-digit inflation and slow disinflation
notes.summary: The OECD reported a return to double-digit consumer price inflation and projected slow disinflation.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2017 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 3. Developments in individual OECD and selected non-member economies > Turkey
source.quote: Consumer price inflation is back in double digits and disinflation is projected to be slow.

notes.title: Lira weakness persisted despite higher interest rates
notes.summary: The OECD described a highly volatile exchange rate and substantial recent lira depreciation despite an increase in the policy interest rate.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2018 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: Chapter 3. Developments in individual OECD and selected non-member economies > Turkey
source.quote: The exchange rate remains highly volatile, with the lira depreciating substantially recently despite a significant increase in the policy interest rate

notes.title: Policy rate raised sharply to 24%
notes.summary: The CBRT Monetary Policy Committee increased the one-week repo auction rate from 17.75% to 24%.

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2018-38)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee
source.quote: has decided to increase the policy rate (one week repo auction rate) from 17.75 percent to 24 percent.

notes.title: Recovery projected, conditional on confidence holding
notes.summary: The OECD projected a measured recovery from the second half of 2019, conditional on no new shocks to international or domestic confidence.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2019 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: 3 Developments in individual OECD and selected non-member economies > Turkey
source.quote: Absent any new shocks to international and domestic confidence, a measured recovery is projected from the second half of 2019 onwards

notes.title: Policy rate cut to 19.75%
notes.summary: The CBRT Monetary Policy Committee reduced the one-week repo auction rate from 24% to 19.75%.

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2019-29)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee
source.quote: has decided to reduce the policy rate (one-week repo auction rate) from 24 percent to 19.75 percent.

notes.title: Renewed lockdowns posed a sharper output risk
notes.summary: In its double-hit pandemic scenario, the OECD warned that renewed lockdowns would cause a sharper decline in Turkish investment and output during 2020.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2020 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: 3 Developments in individual OECD and selected non-member economies > Turkey
source.quote: In the double-hit scenario, renewed lockdown measures would lead to a sharper investment and output decline in 2020

notes.title: Policy rate raised to 15%
notes.summary: The CBRT Monetary Policy Committee increased the one-week repo auction rate from 10.25% to 15%.

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2020-68)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee
source.quote: increase the policy rate (one-week repo auction rate) from 10.25 percent to 15 percent

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2021-13)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee

notes.title: OECD projected 5.7% growth, absent further major shocks
notes.summary: Conditional on the absence of further major shocks, the OECD projected GDP growth of 5.7% in 2021 and 3.4% in 2022.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2021 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: 2. Developments in individual OECD and selected non-member economies > Turkey
source.quote: In the absence of further major shocks, GDP growth is projected to be 5.7% in 2021 before easing to 3.4% in 2022.

notes.title: Policy rate reduced to 14%
notes.summary: The CBRT Monetary Policy Committee reduced the one-week repo auction rate from 15% to 14%.

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2021-59)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee
source.quote: has decided to reduce the policy rate (one-week repo auction rate) from 15 percent to 14 percent.

notes.title: OECD projected inflation above 70% in 2022
notes.summary: The OECD projected consumer inflation above 70% in 2022, citing accommodative monetary policy and high commodity and food prices.

source.title: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 1 — Türkiye
source.section: 2 Developments in individual OECD and selected non-member economies > Türkiye
source.quote: Accommodative monetary policy coupled with high commodity and food prices will keep consumer inflation above 70% in 2022.

notes.title: Policy rate reduced to 9%
notes.summary: The CBRT Monetary Policy Committee reduced the one-week repo auction rate from 10.5% to 9%.

source.title: Press Release on Interest Rates (2022-47)
source.section: Decision of the Monetary Policy Committee
source.quote: has decided to reduce the policy rate (one-week repo auction rate) from 10.5 percent to 9 percent.

notes.title: OECD recommended carefully communicated rate increases
